question: What first round vote share will José Maria Neves win in the 2026 Cape Verdean presidential election?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Cape Verdean presidents seeking re-election (Pires 2006 51%, Fonseca 2016 74%), plus Neves's 2021 run of 51.7% when his party polled only ~38% in parliament. PAICV won the May 2026 legislative vote 48.0-44.8; MpD lost and its leader resigned; the new PM backs Neves; challenger Joana Rosa was a minister in the defeated government. Four minor candidates likely take 3-7% combined. No published polls exist. Polymarket prices Neves to WIN (either round) at 0.83 on ~$23k volume — a different contract (win vs first-round share), so it is a loose check that hints at more downside, not an anchor. No Kalshi/Manifold/bookmaker market found. Overall median ~57%; ~35% chance he tops 60%.
calls.dossier:
- Election 15 Nov 2026; runoff 29 Nov if nobody gets >50% (Wikipedia, 2026 CV presidential election page). Resolves off the CNE-declared first-round percentage for Neves.
- Event window: first round 15 Nov 2026 -> result declared, annulled if no result by 31 Dec 2026; as of 2026-10-25 the vote has not happened (0% of the voting window elapsed).
- Six candidates admitted by the Constitutional Court (Expresso das Ilhas 22 Sep 2026; Balai, Acórdão 80/2026 of 24 Sep): José Maria Neves (incumbent, PAICV), Joana Rosa (former justice minister 2021-26, MpD-backed), Gilson Alves (doctor, 0.76% in 2021), Casimiro de Pina (jurist), Antero Tavares (judge), Loisito Tavares de Sousa (lecturer). Five other bids were rejected.
- May 17, 2026 parliamentary election: PAICV 48.04% / 37 seats, MpD 44.75% / 33 seats, UCID 2 seats; turnout 46.5%. MpD leader Ulisses Correia e Silva resigned; PAICV's Francisco Carvalho became PM (Wikipedia).
- PM Carvalho publicly endorsed Neves (Jornal Económico, Sep/Oct 2026).
- 2021 presidential: Neves 51.7% (as an opposition-party candidate) vs Carlos Veiga (MpD) ~42%, others ~6% combined; in the April 2021 legislative vote PAICV took ~38% vs MpD ~50%, so Neves ran 12+ pts ahead of his party.
- Historical: 2006 incumbent Pires 50.98% vs Veiga 49.02% (two-way race); 2016 incumbent Fonseca ~74% with no major-party opponent; 2011 open seat, first round split 37.8/32.5/27.8.
- Arguments up: incumbency, his party governing (~6 months in), MpD demoralised after defeat, Rosa tied to the defeated government, his record of outperforming the party.
- Arguments down: MpD base still ~45% in May; Rosa pitches 'renewal' and first woman president (A Nação commentary 22 Sep 2026); low turnout adds variance; four minor candidates split off a few points; new government could face early dissatisfaction.
- Searched and absent: any published poll for the 2026 presidential race; Kalshi/Manifold/bookmaker markets. Polymarket has only win/lose contracts (either round), not a vote-share contract.

calls.reasoning: Incumbent Neves (PAICV, which won the May 2026 legislatives 48.0 vs 44.8) faces MpD-backed ex-minister Joana Rosa plus four minor candidates taking ~4-6%. Two-bloc structure: MpD-aligned presidential candidates have taken ~42%+ whenever contested. Neves got 51.7% in 2021 as a non-incumbent against a stronger opponent, Veiga. Incumbency, the new government's honeymoon and MpD's demoralisation point to a median of ~55-56 overall, but clearing 60 needs the MpD vote to fall to ~35%. Polymarket's 0.83 win price (covers both rounds, thin) also argues against an overconfident upper tail. No polls exist.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the facts: six admitted candidates, the May 2026 result of PAICV 48.04 vs MpD 44.75, Neves's 51.7% in 2021, no polls, and Polymarket at 0.83 on a win-in-either-round contract. The minor gap on final ballot names was settled by two dossiers citing the TC/CNE list of six; it is immaterial to the forecast. The core dispute was judgment: the size of the >60% tail (0.20/0.35/0.40) and the median (~55-59). I weighted the two-bloc structure (MpD-aligned candidates at 42%+ in every contested race; MpD's 44.8% in May) and the thin market's 0.83 win price, which implies real chance of a runoff or loss. That puts a landslide above 60 at ~23%, below the two higher runs, and the overall median at ~56. No web access on this run; nothing retrieved.

disagreements.verdict: Set at 0.23: bloc structure and MpD's 44.8% in May make a sub-35% MpD showing unlikely, though possible
~56: incumbency boost over 2021's 51.7%, limited by the MpD base and the market's implied runoff risk
